Personality: Mimir is widely regarded as a man as cold as the northern ice and snow. Inheriting his father Raganvad's harsh and unyielding temperament, he is utterly devoid of empathy in his dealings with others and proves quite parsimonious when rewarding subordinates. Taking little interest in chasing illusory honor or a name for martial valor, he prefers to view warfare through a pragmatic lens. Rather than charging at the front of the battle line, he excels at standing behind stout city walls and using precise engineering knowledge and rigorous tactical deployments to break the enemy. A man of few words whose cold, expressionless eyes are constantly calculating gains and losses, this near-cruel composure makes him feared even at the age of eighteen. Knowing full well how fragile power can be, he places his trust in cold steel, stout fortresses, and efficient administration far more than in the hollow professions of loyalty on the lips of the boyars.
Background: As the son of Grand Prince Raganvad of Sturgia and Asta, Mimir was born into the illustrious Gundaroving clan. Growing up amid the biting winds of Varcheg, he witnessed how his father leveraged his mother's family ties and close connection to the Skolderbrotva to keep the scheming boyars in check. As a member of the high nobility, he received a strict military and administrative education from childhood, displaying remarkable talent in engineering construction, tactical command, and estate governance. In the Grand Principality of Sturgia—a realm evolved from a loose confederation where the seeds of rebellion lie buried deep—he understands that only absolute authority and impregnable defenses can sustain rule. Steadfastly loyal to his father Raganvad, and drawing upon the administrative experience he has accumulated in fiefs such as Mazhadan Castle and Balgard, he stands ready to use his cold wisdom to build an unbreachable line of defense for a kingdom struggling under Imperial pressure.
